Listen to this article Share The Aesthetic Clinic (TAC) and Rejuva Skincare are set to spotlight skin health, confidence, and cultural expression at Wear Your Skin Lagos, an event scheduled for November 21, 2026, combining clinical skincare education, fashion and entertainment. The event, which follows previous editions in London and Manchester, aims to promote informed skincare practices and celebrate melanin-rich skin while addressing common concerns such as acne, hyperpigmentation, dark spots, and uneven skin tone. Organisers said the Lagos edition would provide a platform for conversations around skin health, with professional consultations, skin assessments, and live treatment demonstrations led by TAC doctors. The programme will also feature question-and-answer session, allowing attendees to seek guidance on skincare concerns in an open setting. The initiative comes amid growing interest in skincare solutions tailored to different skin tones, particularly among people seeking to manage pigmentation and other common skin conditions. Beyond clinical education, the event will explore the relationship between skin health, personal identity, and confidence, challenging perceptions that healthy skin must be flawless. “Wear Your Skin is about helping people feel confident in the skin they’re in. Your skin doesn’t need to be perfect to deserve care and celebration, and we’re proud to bring this experience home to Lagos,” said Ifeoma Abajue of The Aesthetic Clinic. A major highlight will be the official launch of TAC Passport, a membership benefit designed for eligible TAC package members. The programme is intended to extend membership benefits across participating clinic locations in the United Kingdom, Canada, and Ghana, subject to applicable terms. Rejuva Skincare will also unveil a new body hyperpigmentation range designed to address dark spots and uneven skin tone, extending its focus on targeted skincare solutions for melanin-rich skin beyond facial care. Fashion will feature prominently through a runway showcase involving Lagos designers, with collections presented in nude, brown, and earth tones. Models representing different skin tones and body types will reinforce the event’s message of inclusivity and self-expression. The programme will also feature personal accounts from individuals sharing their experiences with skin confidence, alongside a live performance by magician FaddoTheGreat. Shopping, refreshments, networking, and photography opportunities will form part of the event, bringing together skincare professionals, fashion enthusiasts, and members of the public. Through its blend of medical guidance, product innovation, and cultural expression, Wear Your Skin Lagos seeks to encourage more inclusive conversations about skincare and reinforce the importance of appropriate care for different skin types and tones. Chinwe Michael Chinwe Michael is a Nigerian business journalist and media professional with over 4 years of experience covering companies, financial markets, banking, fintech, economic policy, financial inclusion, and corporate affairs. She currently leads the Companies & Markets desk at BusinessDay, where she drives coverage of Nigeria’s corporate and capital markets, translates complex financial data into accessible stories, and mentors younger journalists. Prior to that, she was the head of the financial inclusion/fintech desk. With a background in banking and finance and extensive experience in media and communications, Michael has developed expertise in financial journalism, economic analysis, investigative reporting and market intelligence. Her work examines how monetary policy, corporate performance, capital flows, technology, and regulatory decisions affect businesses, investors, and households. She was selected from about 3,000 applicants as one of 20 journalists for Cohort 4 of the MTN Media Innovation Programme, gaining exposure to new approaches to journalism, technology, and media innovation. Her international journalism experience and engagement with professionals across Russia, Dubai, Saudi Arabia, and others in different sectors have further broadened her understanding of global communication and development.
